# nebula_certificate (Resource)

A Nebula host certificate signed by a CA whose key lives in transit. Creating it needs `read` on `<mount>/keys/<key_name>` and `update` on `<mount>/sign/<key_name>`. Reading and deleting it never call OpenBao/Vault. Any change to an input replaces the certificate, except `early_renewal_hours`.

The validity never exceeds the CA's: a `duration` that would is capped to the CA's `not_after` (like `nebula-cert sign`), while an explicit `not_after` past the CA's is an error.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "nebula_certificate" "lighthouse" {
  ca_cert_pem = nebula_ca.mesh.cert_pem
  key_name    = nebula_ca.mesh.key_name
  key_version = nebula_ca.mesh.key_version

  # From nebula_keypair, or from `nebula-cert keygen` run on the host.
  public_key_pem = nebula_keypair.lighthouse.public_key_pem

  name     = "lighthouse-1"
  networks = ["10.99.0.1/16"]
  groups   = ["lighthouse"]
  duration = "720h"

  # Replace the certificate when less than 10 days are left.
  early_renewal_hours = 240
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `ca_cert_pem` (String) The CA certificate (one certificate, not a bundle), usually `nebula_ca.<name>.cert_pem`. Its public key must equal the public key of `key_name` version `key_version`.
- `key_name` (String) Name of the `ed25519` transit key that holds the CA private key.
- `key_version` (Number) Version of the transit key to sign with. Pinned on purpose: rotating the transit key creates a new CA, which must be rolled out with a CA bundle (see the README).
- `name` (String) Name of the certificate.
- `networks` (List of String) Nebula addresses of the host with the overlay prefix length, e.g. `10.99.0.2/24`. Version 1 certificates support exactly one IPv4 network.
- `public_key_pem` (String) The host's X25519 public key in Nebula PEM format, from `nebula_keypair` or `nebula-cert keygen` on the host.

### Optional

- `duration` (String) Validity as a Go duration, e.g. `720h`. Capped to the CA's `not_after`. If neither `duration` nor `not_after` is set, the certificate expires with the CA. Conflicts with `not_after`.
- `early_renewal_hours` (Number) Plan a replacement this many hours before `not_after`. The check runs during plan, so renewal happens on the first apply inside the window. Defaults to `0` (replace once expired). Changing it alone does not replace the certificate.
- `groups` (List of String) Groups of the host, for firewall rules.
- `not_after` (String) Expiry as an RFC 3339 timestamp with whole seconds. Unlike `duration` it is never capped: a value after the CA's `not_after` is an error. If not set, computed.
- `unsafe_networks` (List of String) Unsafe networks (CIDR) this host routes for.
- `version` (Number) Nebula certificate format version, `1` or `2`. Defaults to `2`. Version 2 needs Nebula 1.10 or newer.

### Read-Only

- `cert_pem` (String) The certificate in Nebula PEM format.
- `fingerprint` (String) SHA-256 fingerprint of the certificate, as shown by `nebula-cert print`.
- `id` (String) The certificate fingerprint.
- `not_before` (String) Start of validity (RFC 3339).
- `ready_for_renewal` (Boolean) True when the certificate is expired or within `early_renewal_hours` of expiry; the plan then replaces it.
